script.title: Lessee day-one: ROU asset and lease liability
script.caption_hook: A lessee books an asset it doesn't own. Here's why, with numbers.

lines.say: Why book an asset for something we don't even own?
You get a right to use the asset and an obligation to make lease payments. So book an ROU asset and a lease liability.
Which one do we calculate first?
Liability first: the present value of unpaid lease payments, at the implicit rate or else IBR.

board.title: Lease liability
board.sub: P = unpaid payment; r = rate; t = period

lines.say: So IBR isn't used every time?
Correct. Implicit rate first; IBR only otherwise.
Lease: three years, ₹10,000 at each year end, 10% per annum implicit rate. Direct costs ₹1,000, incentive ₹500, no restoration.
Liability plus prepaid payments, direct costs and restoration, minus incentives received.

board.title: ROU asset at cost
board.formula: ROU = LL + LP + D + R − I
board.sub: LP prepaid; D costs; R restore; I incentive

lines.say: Oh, incentive is minus! So what's the total here?
Debit ROU asset ₹25,369. Credit lease liability ₹24,869 and cash ₹500, which is ₹1,000 paid minus ₹500 incentive.
Remember: liability is the base, and the ROU asset adds the extras.

check_notes: Writer: Example: 3 years, ₹10,000 at each year end, implicit rate 10% p.a. (annuity factor 2.4869 gives ₹24,869). ROU = 24,869 + 1,000 direct costs - 500 incentive = ₹25,369; incentive assumed received in cash at commencement, so net cash is ₹500. Journal line on board abbreviated to 'Lease Liab.' to fit 24 characters. Teacher line 2 trimmed to the 22-word limit while keeping the examiner's wording.

Checker: Whole script (title, Line 2 or Line 4): the standard is never named. ROU-asset accounting for lessees comes from Ind AS 116, not AS 19. AS 19 has no ROU asset and treats operating leases as rent expense. Add it, e.g. 'Under Ind AS 116, book an ROU asset and a lease liability.'

Checker: Line 7 and its board ('Incentive ₹500'): it doesn't say when or how the incentive is received. Lines 13–14 assume it is received in cash at commencement and netted against the ₹1,000 paid. Say so: 'Lease incentive ₹500 received in cash at commencement; initial direct costs ₹1,000 paid at commencement.' Otherwise the cash credit of ₹500 doesn't follow from the facts given.

Checker: Line 7 and its board ('Direct costs paid ₹1,000'), and Line 11 (D = costs): use the Ind AS 116 term 'initial direct costs incurred by the lessee'. Line 11 should also say 'lease incentives received', and the restoration item is an 'estimate of dismantling/restoration costs'.

Checker: Line 4 and Line 6: 'IBR' is never expanded. The rule is to use the lessee's incremental borrowing rate when the interest rate implicit in the lease cannot be readily determined. Suggested wording: 'IBR only if the implicit rate can't be readily determined.'

Checker: Line 9: the annuity factor 2.4869 is right (0.9091 + 0.8264 + 0.7513). The exact present value is ₹24,868.52, so you could add 'rounded'. All other arithmetic checks out: 24,869 + 1,000 − 500 = 25,369, and the journal balances (24,869 + 500 = 25,369).
